# Yongwang walks into a defense, military & security firm

Somewhere right now, in a defense, military & security office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Yongwang**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Underwater Palace.** Yongwang is believed to live in a magnificent palace beneath the sea, where he keeps treasures, controls the tides, and commands armies of fish, turtles, and dragons.  Fishermen who offended Yongwang risked storms and empty nets.

**The Yongwang-gut.** Coastal communities held Yongwang-gut, shamanic rituals dedicated to the dragon king.  Offerings of rice, fruit, and specially prepared food were set afloat or presented on the shore to secure calm seas and abundant catches.

## Not the First Rebrand

Yongwang is part of a broader East Asian dragon-king tradition, with close parallels in Chinese, Japanese, and Vietnamese religion.  In Korea the figure was absorbed into both Buddhism and shamanism, appearing as a donor or protector in Buddhist temples and as a sovereign spirit in gut rituals. The office is only the latest translation.
